Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

glance verb and noun

also glance at, a glance, at first glance, glance over, quick look, at a glance

classical

Cic. Clu. 54; Lael. 9 (Lewis & Short, s.v. conjiciō)
Tac. H. 1.17 (Lewis & Short)

oculōs conjicere in (+ acc.)

cast one’s eyes on, glance at

To turn one’s eyes on someone or something, often for a moment.

Other words

  • strictim aspicere — glance over, look at cursorily

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.162 (Lewis & Short, s.v. strictim)

    Lewis & Short: Ciceronian, but very rare; strictim is “grazingly, in passing”.

  • aspectus, aspectūs m. — a glance, a look

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 200; Cic. Att. 7.3.1 (Lewis & Short)

    At a glance is ūnō aspectū; at first glance, prīmō aspectū.

Examples

  • intellegēns dīcendī exīstimātor ūnō aspectū et praeteriēns dē ōrātōre saepe jūdicat

    an expert judge of speaking often makes up his mind about a speaker at a single glance, in passingCic. Brut. 200 (Lewis & Short)

  • ē quibus prīmō aspectū voluptātem cēpī, quod erant ā tē ipsō scrīptae

    at first glance your letters gave me pleasure, because they were written in your own handCic. Att. 7.3.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also look at me, survey, see.
